For the odd-parity mode $(\ell,m)=(2,1)$, we compute the waveform numerically and derive an analytic expression for the EP contribution to the ringdown waveform directly from the particle source. Comparison with the numerical waveform shows that the particle excites the EP response, which, together with its mirror contribution, dominates the intermediate ringdown stage. We use waveform fitting and Bayesian analysis to assess the limitations of conventional QNM templates for EP ringdown. In the fitting, the EP template recovers the complex frequency $ω$ more accurately than the ordinary template. In Bayesian analysis, at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $ρ=100$, the ordinary template yields a narrow frequency posterior whose $90\%$ credible region excludes the true EP frequency, whereas the broader EP-template region contains it. The Bayes factor nevertheless favors the ordinary template at lower SNRs and the EP template only at higher SNRs. These results show that in the EP case a narrow posterior and favorable Bayesian evidence do not guarantee accurate frequency inference when a conventional template omits the characteristic EP ringdown structure.

entries.title: Stellar Loci XI: Identifications and Parameter Determinations of Binary Stars by multi-band photometry
entries.abstract: Large photometric surveys contain numerous unresolved binaries, but identifying them and measuring component properties remains challenging. We present a 65-band UV-to-IR SED-fitting framework to identify unresolved main-sequence binaries and infer their parameters. Photometry combines synthetic miniJPAS magnitudes from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra with 2MASS and WISE measurements. Using LAMOST-calibrated, metallicity-dependent stellar loci and a dwarf-star color-absolute-magnitude relation, we construct forward models for single stars and unresolved binaries. We fit both model families to each SED with MCMC, using Gaia distances as Hertzsprung-Russell-diagram constraints to infer metallicity, reddening, and component photometric parameters. Component masses and mass ratios are derived from PARSEC models. Simulations show the method robustly recovers binary parameters. Tests on a LAMOST comparison sample indicate sensitivity to binaries with $q\gtrsim0.4$; the preferred model reproduces spectroscopic metallicities with 0.11 dex scatter, while inferred reddenings agree with external extinction maps with $\sim0.02$ mag scatter. Comparison with an external Gaia XP-based binary catalog shows broadly consistent binary classifications for common sources. Our metallicities more closely follow the LAMOST spectroscopic scale, and mass-ratio estimates in the intermediate-$q$ regime better trace expected $Δ$-HRD offsets. Tests using M67 members support internal consistency of inferred parameters. For quality-selected Gaia non-single-star binaries, primary-mass estimates agree with Gaia NSS values with 0.071 $M_\odot$ residual scatter; in cases with larger discrepancies, further tests indicate that secondary-mass and mass-ratio estimates are more reliable than the Gaia NSS values. The method scales to large photometric samples, enabling population studies and analyses of individual systems.

entries.title: EP250226a: A fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A and its multiwavelength afterglow properties
entries.abstract: Recent advances in fast X-ray transient studies have been driven by the wide-field, sensitive soft X-ray monitoring capabilities of the Einstein Probe (EP), enabling the prompt detection and localization of previously underexplored events. EP observations offer new opportunities to investigate the origins, emission mechanisms, and population properties of newly discovered fast X-ray transients. We present multiwavelength observations of EP250226a, an extragalactic fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A. We jointly analyze the prompt emission from soft X-rays to gamma rays and the X-ray afterglow spectra. We collect optical photometric data, perform empirical and afterglow model-based analyses, and present optical-to-infrared spectroscopy, measuring the equivalent widths of absorption lines. The spectroscopic redshift is $z = 3.314$, and the isotropic-equivalent gamma-ray energy is $E_\mathrm{iso}\simeq7.32\times10^{53}$ erg. Its location in the Amati diagram is consistent with a massive-star core-collapse origin (Type II GRB). The fluence ratio $\rm{S}(25-50\,\rm{keV})/\rm{S}(50-100\,\rm{keV})=0.57\pm0.06$ supports its classification as a classical GRB. The X-ray and optical afterglows show achromatic behavior. Among the models considered, a top-hat jet propagating into a uniform interstellar medium best describes the multiwavelength afterglow. This model suggests a highly collimated, nearly on-axis jet, with an isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of $E_\mathrm{k,iso}\simeq4.07\times10^{55}$ erg, a gamma-ray radiative efficiency of $η_γ\simeq 1.77\%$, and a low magnetic-field energy fraction of $\log ε_\mathrm{B,FS} \simeq -6.52$. EP250226a exhibits typical long-duration GRB properties, with the first soft X-ray peak coinciding with the gamma-ray prompt emission, while the soft X-ray emission lasts significantly longer than the gamma-ray emission.

entries.title: Polarized transport in a Thomson slab: Stokes recursion, asymptotic eigenmodes, and Comptonization applications
entries.abstract: We develop a scattering-order-resolved Stokes-vector recursion for axisymmetric polarized transport in a finite plane-parallel Thomson slab. The post-scattering radiation field closes exactly within two depth-dependent coefficients, yielding escape probabilities, angular distributions and linear polarization while conserving photon number. At high scattering orders, the principal eigenmode of the weighted self-adjoint transport operator controls the escape statistics, and the normalized angular distribution and polarization become independent of the seed source. The subdominant spectrum quantifies convergence, with the characteristic scattering order scaling as the square of the optical depth in thick slabs. We derive logarithmic corrections to the thin-slab complete-polarization limit away from the slab normal, together with a finite-optical-depth Galerkin approximation. In optically thick slabs, matching bulk diffusion to a polarized Milne surface layer yields finite-thickness corrections to the Chandrasekhar solution. We provide compact formulae for the principal and leading subdominant eigenvalues and the asymptotic angular and polarization distributions across both regimes. Combining the recursion with an angle-averaged thermal-Compton redistribution kernel gives approximate energy-resolved Stokes spectra. Comparisons with full polarized Compton calculations show that this separable reconstruction is most reliable for cool, optically thick media. Applied to the non-dipping observations of neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary system 4U 1624-49, the model provides acceptable joint fits to the broadband intensity and IXPE Stokes spectra, showing that an extended corona overlying the accretion disc can account for the observed X-ray polarization.

entries.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The PHZ processing function for the physical properties of galaxies
entries.abstract: Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.

entries.title: The Black Hole Mass of the Sunflower Galaxy NGC 5055: Direct Measurement via Stellar Kinematics with Keck/OSIRIS Laser Guide Star Adaptive Optics
entries.abstract: We present the first stellar-dynamical supermassive black hole mass measurement in the nearby spiral galaxy NGC 5055 (M63) using near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy with Keck/OSIRIS assisted by the laser guide star adaptive optics system. The observations deliver two-dimensional stellar kinematics extracted from the CO bandhead absorption features via pPXF at an angular resolution of $0.045''$. The stellar velocity dispersion rises steeply from $\sim90~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$ at $r\sim1''$ to a central peak of $\sim135~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$, kinematically tracing the gravitational influence of a central mass concentration. Modeling these kinematics with an ensemble of four JAM models, spanning cylindrical and spherical velocity-ellipsoid alignments and two independent MGE decompositions of archival HST imaging, yields a black hole mass of $M_{\rm BH}=4.56^{+1.73}_{-1.82}\times10^6~{\rm M_\odot}$. The stellar orbits are consistent with near-isotropy ($β\approx0$), typical of rotating late-type galaxies. NGC 5055 emerges as a remarkable local analogue to the Milky Way in terms of its black hole, nuclear star cluster, and total stellar mass. The surface brightness profile of NGC 5055 shows no evidence for a classical bulge; if confirmed bulgeless, NGC 5055 would join the rare class of spirals with a direct dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ determination in the absence of a bulge, a regime currently populated by only a handful of galaxies including NGC 2748 and NGC 4395. This measurement provides a new anchor for black hole scaling relations in late-type galaxies at the low-mass end of the black hole mass spectrum.

entries.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) - First NISP emission-line maps: Methodology, validation, and applications to galaxy evolution
entries.abstract: We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$α$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$α$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$α$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$α$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$α$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}α}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

entries.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Colouring Euclid with external ground-based imaging data
entries.abstract: Accurate photometric-redshift estimation and calibration of the weak-lensing point-spread function (PSF) for Euclid require complementary ground-based optical imaging with high photometric precision and spatial homogeneity. The Organisation Unit for External Data (OU-EXT) integrates heterogeneous ground-based surveys into the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), delivering uniformly calibrated, co-added images, and associated PSF models. To minimise systematics in spectral energy distribution (SED) reconstruction and photometric-redshift estimation, these data must achieve relative photometric stability at the $\sim$10 mmag level on Euclid-tile scales. We present the ground-based imaging component of Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), comprising $\sim2500$ deg$^2$ across the wide, deep, and auxiliary fields. We summarise the OU-EXT production workflow and validation framework, and quantify the achieved data quality of the co-added products in terms of depth, photometric zero-point stability, and spatial colour homogeneity. In the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS), the point-source $10σ$ depths in the $griz$ bands reach 24.8/24.3/24.0/23.0 AB mag, with the deep fields extending 1--2 magnitudes deeper. Most EWS DR1 tiles meet the 10 mmag relative photometric requirement, with 1.1% and 1.5% showing offsets exceeding 50 mmag in the northern and southern hemispheres, respectively. Spatial colour variations remain typically below 5--10 mmag across the southern EWS footprint, while larger residual structures of 10--25 mmag appear in some northern regions. These results demonstrate that the EXT production chain provides a largely homogeneous framework for integrating ground-based datasets into Euclid, while identifying calibration and co-addition limitations that have to be addressed in DR2 to meet the mission's most stringent cosmological requirements. (Abridged)

entries.title: Self-Organizing Maps for the Exploration and Classification of X-Ray Sources in the Chandra Source Catalog
entries.abstract: In this work, we apply Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to the Chandra Source Catalog (CSC) to investigate the distribution of observation-level detections in the feature space defined by their spectral and variability properties. SOMs are neural-network-based models that project points in high-dimensional space onto a two-dimensional latent space while preserving their local topological structure. From CSC 2.1.1 we extract a sample of 36,904 ACIS-only, observation-level, high statistical significance detections, belonging to 17,927 unique sources. Among these detections, 25,192 (10,078 sources) are associated with a label from SIMBAD via a 1" cross-match that provides information about their astrophysical nature. Training a 40x40 hexagonal SOM reveals structured regions in the U-Matrix and activation response map, and feature-projection maps trace coherent patterns in spectral shape and variability. Overlaying SIMBAD classes shows that labeled populations occupy distinct, partially adjacent regions of the map and that generic categories can be interpreted via their SOM locations. We then retrain the SOM for classification using a source-grouped train/validation/test split and introduce SOMClassifier. When applied to 11,712 detections without SIMBAD labels, it assigns valid (non-abstained) labels to 6,225 detections (coverage ~53%). Furthermore, we release the trained models and visualization/classification workflows through a public web application built on the most up-to-date CSC release.

entries.title: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multi-task galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
entries.abstract: Inferring photometric redshifts ($z$) and key stellar population properties ($\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $D_n4000$, and $\mathrm{H}δ_A$) directly from multi-band imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional point-wise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts non-linear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tail populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band ($g,r,i,z,y$) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: $σ_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.020$ for $z$, $0.169\,\mathrm{dex}$ for $\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $0.073$ for $D_n4000$, and $1.185\,\text{Å}$ for $\mathrm{H}δ_A$. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (RMSE changes $\le 3.5\%$) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era.

entries.title: Dissecting and diagnosing the LISA Galactic binary population
entries.abstract: LISA will individually resolve thousands of Galactic double white dwarf (DWD) binaries, while the majority stays buried in an unresolved gravitational wave (GW) confusion foreground. Which systems get resolved depends on the binary's parameters, on the global population and on instrumental sensitivity, so the resolved population is not a representative sample of the underlying Galactic population. Interpreting LISA's future catalog therefore requires understanding these selection effects. Here we characterize the resolved and unresolved subpopulations of a simulated Milky Way DWD catalog, using an iterative subtraction pipeline applied over different observation times. Resolvability is driven primarily by chirp mass: higher chirp mass, inspiraling systems are strongly favored over lower mass, outspiraling or monochromatic ones, and this reflects on the rate with which different composition subtypes are resolved. Spatially, resolved sources trace the Galactic bulge, because it is intrinsically the densest region of the Galaxy. The confusion background shows an internal bimodal chirp-mass structure, and is not generated uniformly by the same subpopulation in different frequency bands. We introduce a diagnostic for the minimum number of sources needed to reproduce a given fraction of the confusion power in a frequency band, and show that a residual confusion floor persists even after 100 years of integration. These biases are significant and need to be accounted for when using LISA's resolved DWD catalog and the confusion background to constrain the Galactic DWD population.

entries.title: Revisiting the Isospin Quartic Term of the Nucleonic Matter Equation of State in the Walecka Model
entries.abstract: The fourth-order nuclear symmetry energy $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)$ is generally regarded as a small correction to the quadratic symmetry energy, but its magnitude, density dependence, and implications for neutron stars (NSs) remain unconstrained. Within the nonlinear Walecka model, we derive an analytical expression for $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)$ and construct 3000 equations of state (EOSs) constrained by nuclear data and astrophysical observations. We find that: (1) At saturation density, $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ_0)$ can reach $6$\,MeV or higher, well above the commonly expected $2$\,MeV, while relatively large values can remain compatible with microscopic calculations. (2) Over NS densities, $|E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)|$ generally stays below $20$\,MeV but can reach about $25\%$ of the symmetry energy. (3) EOSs with $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ_0)\gtrsim2\,\rm{MeV}$ can exhibit positive symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ while satisfying the GW170817 tidal deformability constraint, potentially relaxing the previously inferred preference for negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$. (4) The density derivatives of $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)$, particularly its curvature $K_{\rm{sym,4}}$, can contribute substantially to the fourth-order isospin incompressibility. (5) Variations in $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ_0)$ across selected EOSs can change the low-density squared speed of sound by $40\%$ or more. Higher-order symmetry energies also affect the proton fraction and NS core-crust transition. Thus, even a modest fourth-order contribution to the EOS can significantly influence the response and composition of asymmetric nucleonic matter, highlighting the importance of going beyond the quadratic approximation.

entries.title: Residual ellipticity driven by intense magnetic stress in the hot neutron star era
entries.abstract: A neutron star with a nonaxisymmetric mass distribution continuously radiates gravitational waves. The amplitude depends on the magnitude of the deformation, and is crucial for gravitational-wave astronomy. We studied an evolutionary effect on the magnetically induced ellipticity in the neutron star crust. A large deformation at the hot era before solidification is assumed to be produced magneto-hydrodynamically, and the fate at later time follows owing to the decrease in the force associated with the decay and redistribution of the current. Instead of simulating the evolution of deformation with the magnetic field over a long timescale, we estimate the ellipticity that remains after the formation of the solid crust by comparing two equilibrium models before and after solidification. The relic ellipticity is $\sim 10^{-8} (B_0/10^{13}{\rm{G}})^2$ in the magnitude for dipole field strength $B_{0}$ at the surface. This value was primarily determined by the magnetic field at the later time, with a weak dependence on the initial large deformation. The memory of the presolidification state was retained, but was small because the elastic force contributes little to the equilibrium.

entries.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
entries.abstract: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the strongest and most efficient jet, as it accumulates the most magnetic flux at the black hole horizon. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $σ\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $Γ_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.

entries.title: Solar models using OPLIB monochromatic opacities
entries.abstract: Context. Opacity is a key ingredient in describing the transport of energy in stars. There are several methods for calculating stellar opacities, resulting in different tables (OPAL, OP, OPAS, and OPLIB). These opacities are available in two distinct forms: tables that regroup the Rosseland mean opacity pre-calculated at predefined chemical mixtures, and monochromatic opacity spectra of individual chemical elements, which allow for the computation of Rosseland mean opacity for a precise mixture. Aims. This study presents our implementation of the OPLIB monochromatic opacity data in Cesam2k20 and compares the solar-calibrated model obtained with these opacities to helioseismic data in order to evaluate the improvements made by using monochromatic opacities. Methods. We implemented the OPLIB monochromatic opacity data in the Cesam2k20 stellar evolution code following the method already used for the OP monochromatic opacity data. Results. We found that calibrated solar models produced with monochromatic opacity data (OP and OPLIB) agree better overall with helioseismic constraints than those produced with pre-calculated opacity tables.

entries.title: Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and $Λ$CDM simulations
entries.abstract: We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations. Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim53\%$, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues ($\sim17$-$27\%$). This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut ($M_\star > 10^4\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) to match the resolution limits of the simulations. In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim28\%$. However, only a minority of pair candidates exhibit coherent kinematics or are likely to be gravitationally bound, indicating that most represent transient alignments or remnants of common group infall rather than long-lived binary satellites. These results suggest that the MW hosts an unusually rich population of phase-space-correlated satellites, likely reflecting its recent accretion history, whereas M31 is more consistent with typical $Λ$CDM expectations.

entries.title: Dark matter evolution in stellar objects: A Boltzmann transport approach
entries.abstract: Dark matter (DM) captured by stars offers a way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study the evolution of captured DM with the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), which follows both the abundance and the phase-space distribution of the bound particles from capture toward a stationary state. Averaging over orbital motion, we write the BTE as a master equation in energy and angular momentum that includes capture, scattering between bound orbits, annihilation and evaporation. Applying it to the Sun, we find that captured DM does not thermalize within the solar age when its scattering on nuclei is rare. The bound DM then remains much more extended than the isothermal distribution assumed in the classical treatment, and its annihilation rate can be suppressed by many orders of magnitude. We also apply the BTE to the inelastic Higgsino interpretation of the recent LUX-ZEPLIN result, which involves two DM components coupled through inelastic scattering. The thermal motion of solar nuclei opens capture channels that are closed for nuclei at rest and strengthens the constraint on the mass splitting by tens of keV.

entries.title: Efficient Standard Siren Cosmological Inference with Posterior Reuse
entries.abstract: Standard siren cosmology depends on several modelling assumptions, including the underlying source population, galaxy catalogue, and detection selection function. Quantifying the effect of each choice typically requires a full, independent analysis. As gravitational-wave catalogs grow incrementally, much computational effort is spent re-analysing largely overlapping datasets. We apply the recently developed ASPIRE (Accelerated Sequential Posterior Inference via Reuse) sampler to the joint estimation of cosmological and population parameters with dark sirens. ASPIRE updates existing posterior samples into the posterior under a new hypothesis without restarting from the prior. It combines normalising flows with a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to produce accurate posteriors and unbiased evidence estimates. Applying ASPIRE to a number of dark siren analysis cases with GWTC-5.0, we recover posteriors consistent with nested sampling, while recording a performance improvement of between 6-28 times over the set of analyses when using an existing posterior. This enables efficient exploration of modelling choices and rapid updates as catalogs grow, without duplicating existing computational effort.

entries.title: Active Learning for Molecular Discovery: A Retrospective Test toward TMC-1
entries.abstract: Machine-learning recommendation lists can help prioritize searches for new interstellar molecules, but whether reranking such a list as detections accumulate improves on it has not been tested. We present a pre-registered retrospective test toward TMC-1, using a published machine-learning list of 1,510 recommended candidates, consolidated to 1,434 candidates, and the species reported there through September 2026. At four annual origins from 2022 to 2025, a logistic-regression ranking on seven released features, refit on the detections known at each origin, separates later detections from never-detected candidates with a pooled AUC of 0.867, against 0.706 for the best single-criterion baseline (difference 0.160; 95\% interval 0.095-0.230). The advantage persists under a shifted date boundary and two alternative feature regimes, but is not established among the top 100 candidates (12 versus 7 detections). A searcher that refits on its own observations reaches half of the 63 detected species on the list in a median of 200 observations, against 332 for the best fixed ordering and 717.5 expected for random search. Uncertainty sampling, the standard active-learning rule, performs worse than random (AUC 0.210): later detections lie at low predictive uncertainty, close to known chemistry. Of 101 species in our validation set, 37 are absent from the list, and only 13 of these appear in a pool rebuilt from its source databases, including 2 of 11 radicals and neither ion. Candidate generation, not ranking, is the main constraint. We release 100 recommended targets, with code and frozen inputs, for prospective testing.

entries.title: Inertial modes in a turbulent rotating magneto-convection simulation with the solar-like differential rotation
entries.abstract: Recent observations have revealed a variety of solar inertial modes, but their nonlinear properties remain largely unexplored. We aim to identify and characterize inertial modes in a state-of-the-art simulation of rotating magnetoconvection, in which solar-like differential rotation was self-consistently reproduced. We analyzed nine years of high-cadence data from the Hotta (2025) simulation. The spatial eigenfunctions of various low-frequency inertial modes were extracted using singular value decomposition. We identified major classes of retrograde inertial modes, including equatorial Rossby modes, high-latitude modes, and high-frequency retrograde modes, with frequencies and near-surface amplitudes roughly consistent with the solar observations. In particular, thanks to the strongly baroclinic background in the simulation, the observed large amplitude ($\sim 10$ m/s) and the characteristic polar spiral pattern of the high-latitude mode at azimuthal order $m=1$ are successfully reproduced. This indicates that high-latitude modes are excited by baroclinic instability, which can occur even amid turbulent convection. We further show that the prograde columnar modes undergo a qualitative transition at $m \sim 6$, separating the fast-propagating convective modes at $m \gtrsim 6$ from thermally diffusive slow modes at $m \lesssim 6$ whose frequencies closely match recent observational inferences of thermal Rossby modes. Finally, we find that turbulent magnetic fields primarily influence the inertial modes indirectly through modifications of the background state. Our results suggest that the observed properties of solar inertial modes are broadly consistent with a simulation in which solar-like differential rotation is maintained in a magnetically dominated regime, although the simulation still overproduces prograde columnar modes at large $m$.

entries.title: The Same But Different: SiO$_2$ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST
entries.abstract: The precision of brown dwarf spectra from JWST enables unprecedented insight into the atmospheric and cloud properties of sub-stellar atmospheres. Here, we compare both self-consistent radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) and retrieval atmosphere models to high-SNR 1--18~$μ$m spectra of two field L-dwarfs from JWST, J0624 (L5) and J2148 (L6--L6.5). Our observations include spectral features from H$_2$O, CO, CO$_2$, CH$_4$, Na, and K and cover approximately 98\% of the outgoing thermal emission from the two objects. We first compare the data to three independent grids of 1D-RCE models: BT-Settl, exoREM, and Sonora Diamondback. While exoREM provides the best fit of the grid models, no 1D-RCE model provides a satisfactory fit to the data, highlighting the complexity of fitting cloudy L-dwarf spectra. Nonetheless, the temperature and cloud properties can be constrained with the 1D-RCE models, while metallicity, C/O ratio, and surface gravity are not well-measured. Next, we use petitRADTRANS to retrieve atmosphere and cloud properties, finding strong evidence for the presence of SiO$_2$ clouds in both objects. The SiO$_2$ is found to be amorphous in structure for J0624 but crystalline in J2148, highlighting important differences in objects of similar spectral type. We also used a non-Bayesian optimization framework to explore a wider variety of cloud scenarios, finding evidence for the inclusion of iron-rich magnesium silicates (Mg$_{0.5}$Fe$_{0.5}$SiO$_3$, MgFeSiO$_4$) in addition to SiO$_2$ in both objects. These results show both the complexity and diversity of brown dwarf cloud properties, while also highlighting the constraining power of broad-wavelength JWST observations of cloudy L-dwarfs.

entries.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
entries.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $σ/m_χ\sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $σ/m_χ= 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_χ\simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_χ\simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

entries.title: Radiative Transfer Modeling of Multi-Shell Molecular Outflows in the Class 0 Protostar IRAS 15398-3359
entries.abstract: Recent high-angular-resolution observations of protostellar outflows have revealed complex spatial and velocity structures that are difficult to describe with a single shell. We have investigated the primary outflow of the Class 0 protostar IRAS 15398$-$3359 in the H$_2$CO and CS emission observed with ALMA and identified four shell-like components, which trace the cavity walls of the more extended CO outflows. Non-LTE radiative-transfer calculations of H$_2$CO and synthetic ALMA observations of the three-dimensional model show that a common ellipsoidal geometrical form and Hubble-law-like velocity field can broadly reproduce the channel-map and position--velocity structures of the identified shells when the geometry, spatial configuration, and kinematics of each shell are allowed to vary independently. The kinematic timescales and inclination angles of the inner and outer shells are $\sim$1000 yr ($19^\circ$ and $15^\circ$) and $\sim$750 yr ($5^\circ$ and $8^\circ$), respectively. The momentum injection rate of the outer bipolar pair is approximately 2.2 times that of the inner pair. The inferred $\dot{M}_{\rm wind}/\dot{M}_{\rm acc}$ ratios are $0.7$--$3\%$ and $2$--$7\%$ for the inner and outer shells. The observed shell-to-shell differences suggest episodicity of the mass ejection events, where the strength and direction of the outflow activity may vary over short timescales of order $10^2$--$10^3$ yr.

entries.title: Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS): the Outflow-Luminosity Scaling Relations in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds
entries.abstract: Understanding massive star formation in low-metallicity environments is crucial for constraining the universality of star formation across cosmic evolution. In this Letter, we present the first systematic survey of massive protostellar outflows in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC, $Z\sim$0.2--0.5 $Z_\odot$), as part of the Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS). MAGOS targets 40 massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) with luminosities of (1--23)$\times 10^4$ $L_\odot$ with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.85 mm at a linear resolution of $\sim$0.1 pc. Using CO (3--2), we identify blue- and red-shifted outflows associated with the primary continuum sources toward 29 targets in the LMC and 10 targets in the SMC. Comparing the outflow mass, momentum, energy, and force versus luminosity scaling relations in MAGOS with those in the Galaxy, we find that the LMC CO outflows have a similar slope in the mass-luminosity relation, suggesting that CO remains an effective tracer of massive protostellar outflows at $Z\sim$0.5 $Z_\odot$. In contrast, despite the large scatter, the SMC CO outflows are deficient at high luminosity and show flatter scaling relations than the LMC and the Galaxy. This is consistent with reduced CO abundances due to enhanced photodissociation at high luminosity and low metallicity ($Z\sim$0.2 $Z_\odot$), although the possibility of intrinsically weak outflow launching cannot be ruled out with the current data.

entries.title: The $w$-mode instability of strangeon ergostars and its impact on energy extraction
entries.abstract: Rapidly rotating compact ergostars have been proposed as alternative central engines for short gamma-ray bursts. However, competing energy-loss channels, such as gravitational-wave emission driven by non-axisymmetric instabilities, could curtail the power available for relativistic electromagnetic outflows. In this work, we investigate the $w$-mode instability of rapidly rotating strangeon ergostars by solving the coupled spacetime and fluid perturbation equations in the Hilbert gauge using a spectral method, without relying on a slow-rotation approximation. We calculate the complex eigenvalues of the axial-led and polar-led $w$-mode branches originating from the fundamental $l=m=2$ modes of nonrotating stars along the maximum-energy-extraction paths of twelve representative strangeon equations of state. We find that both branches remain damped throughout these paths, despite the presence of ergoregions. We further vary the stellar angular velocity to determine the instability thresholds. In every case with an identified threshold, the angular velocity at the corresponding extraction-path endpoint remains below the critical value, with the largest ratio being $0.926$. Our results indicate that the $w$-mode instabilities examined here do not provide a growing gravitational-wave emission channel along the considered energy-extraction paths, supporting the availability of the previously estimated rotational energy reservoirs for electromagnetic extraction.

entries.title: A deterministic theory of kinetic fluctuations in long-range interacting homogeneous systems without collective effects
entries.abstract: Finite-$N$ fluctuations govern the slow relaxation of long-range interacting systems, yet accessing their full statistics demands huge ensembles of costly simulations. We show that, in homogeneous systems without collective effects, this statistical problem collapses onto just three deterministic kinetic equations. Starting from the Landau-Dean-Kawasaki equation, i.e. the stochastic counterpart of the large deviation principle for the Landau equation, we derive the infinite hierarchy of $n$-point moments of the empirical distribution function at leading order in $1/N$. We prove that it is solved exactly by a quasi-Gaussian closure. The resulting minimal Landau fluctuation hierarchy is formed by the Landau equation, a Lyapunov equation for the two-point moment, and a kinetic equation for the three-point moment. From these three equations, all higher-order moments follow algebraically. The hierarchy exactly preserves the collisional invariants and their fluctuations, and predicts the full probability distribution of observables in the central fluctuation regime. Benchmarked against $N$-body realizations, it reproduces the mean, variance and higher-order moments with an accuracy that improves systematically with $N$. A single deterministic time-integration of three coupled partial differential equations thus replaces large ensembles of simulations, for any large $N$.

entries.title: Lense-Thirring induced repeating blast trains in continuous gravitational waves
entries.abstract: We characterise gravitational lensing induced by the Lense-Thirring effect in a continuous gravitational-wave source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. This scenario is very likely to generate lensing events, as long as the source's orbital inclination is not aligned with the black hole's spin axis and the Lense-Thirring timescale is shorter than the observational window. The signal appears as short-duration ($T_{\rm blast}$) gravitational-wave "blasts" that repeat after every orbit ($T_{\rm orb}$) within a limited time window ($T_{\rm train}$). The blasts' signal strength depends on the system's geometry and not on the black hole mass. The signal will go silent and renew twice in a full Lense-Thirring precession period.

entries.title: Magnetic blue large-amplitude pulsators
entries.abstract: With the discovery of blue large-amplitude pulsators (BLAPs), one of the most important questions to be answered was in which evolutionary channel(s) these radially pulsating stars could form. Located in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram between hot subdwarfs and main sequence, BLAPs cannot be the products of single-star evolution. Therefore, virtually all scenarios explaining their origin assume binarity at some stage of evolution. One of these scenarios proposed that some BLAPs may have formed as a result of the merger of two low-mass white dwarfs or a white dwarf and a main-sequence star. The merger scenario may result in the formation of a magnetic field in the merger product, as is postulated for magnetic white dwarfs. Pulsations in a star with a strong magnetic field can manifest themselves in a way known from rapidly oscillating Ap stars, i.e. in the form of evenly spaced multiplets (usually triplets) in the frequency spectrum. This phenomenon can be explained by the oblique pulsator model. We have shown that the three evenly spaced frequency modes discovered in the first BLAP, OGLE-BLAP-001, can be explained in this way. Similar behaviour has also been found in two other BLAPs.

entries.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
entries.abstract: We present the first systematic parameter-estimation analysis of 42 candidate gravitational-wave signals identified in GWTC-4.0 with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_\mathrm{astro} \geq 0.5$, but a false-alarm rate of at least $1\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which were therefore not selected for parameter estimation in the catalogue. We use a catalogue-style analysis workflow and publicly available strain data to obtain posterior samples for these candidates, of which 29 pass our validation criteria. Of the remaining 13 candidates, seven are consistent with noise or impacted by instrumental artefacts, while six yield results that cannot be reliably interpreted. We identify several interesting candidates: a possible neutron star-black hole merger, GW230920_064709, and two candidates with evidence for non-zero effective spin: GW230902_172430 and GW230823_142524. The latter also shows mild evidence of precession, although further analysis is needed to establish the robustness of this result. We quantify the information gained from these observations using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, finding that the inferred spin parameters are generally only weakly constrained. We present a reproducible analysis workflow that uses publicly available data and software, without access to LVK collaboration resources, and incorporates automated posterior-validation tools. We also provide a data release containing results in a format compatible with those from GWTC-4.0. Our results demonstrate that useful parameter constraints can be obtained for many candidates below the catalogue's parameter-estimation significance threshold, while highlighting the challenges of analysing marginal signals and the importance of careful validation.

entries.title: ALMA quiet Sun observations compared with a simulated MURaM-ChE chromosphere
entries.abstract: Aims. We assess the ability of the MURaM-ChE enhanced network simulation to reproduce the chromospheric millimeter brightness observed with ALMA and investigate the properties of the simulated emission. Methods. We analyze synthetic brightness temperatures from the MURaM-ChE model in ALMA Bands 3 (3.2 mm) and 6 (1.3 mm) and compare them with ALMA observations of quiet-Sun, network, and enhanced network regions. We examine the statistical properties of the brightness distributions, their dependence on magnetic field strength, and their variation with wavelength, using results from Bifrost enhanced network snapshots as additional reference cases. Results. The MURaM-ChE model reproduces the range and variability of brightness temperatures observed in enhanced network regions, with particularly close agreement found for the 23 April 2017 data set. The reference Bifrost snapshots produce lower brightness temperatures in both bands, with values below even those measured by ALMA in the quiet Sun. The systematic offset between the models is present in both bands and is likely associated with differences in atmospheric density stratification and the resulting effective formation heights. Both the observations and simulations show an overall increase in brightness temperature with magnetic field strength and wavelength, although significant scatter is present. Conclusions. The results indicate that the MURaM-ChE model provides a physically consistent representation of chromospheric conditions in enhanced network regions and captures key properties of the observed millimeter emission. The comparison highlights the sensitivity of millimeter brightness to atmospheric stratification and magnetic structure and demonstrates the diagnostic potential of ALMA observations for constraining chromospheric models.

entries.title: A Variable Compact Millimeter Excess in the Type-1 Seyfert Galaxy NGC 985: Implications for a Black-Hole Corona
entries.abstract: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. We present three epochs of ALMA observations of the type-1 Seyfert galaxy NGC 985, together with archival post-upgrade VLA data presented here for the first time, to investigate its compact millimeter excess. The millimeter flux density decreased strongly between the first two ALMA epochs separated by approximately one month, while the component was detected again at an intermediate level in the third epoch. This variability demonstrates an intrinsically variable compact component and implies a model-independent size limit of $\lesssim 0.024$ pc ($\simeq 1.1\times10^3 R_{\rm S}$). Spectral decomposition requires a compact, self-absorbed synchrotron component to reproduce the millimeter-wave data. A hybrid thermal/nonthermal coronal model reproduces the radio-millimeter spectra, with the two broadly sampled ALMA epochs favoring different nonthermal electron distributions. The estimated radiative cooling times are comparable to or shorter than the light-crossing time, implying continuous injection or reacceleration of nonthermal electrons; a change in particle injection is the most natural driver of the observed spectral changes. We conclude that NGC 985 hosts a recurrent and variable compact millimeter synchrotron component. A magnetized corona provides a plausible origin, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish a coronal origin from alternatives such as a jet base.

entries.title: Non-evolutionary effects on period change in Magellanic Cepheids. III. Empirical connection with additional low-amplitude variability
entries.abstract: The O-C method in classical Cepheids traces both evolutionary and shorter-timescale (non-evolutionary) period changes. In our previous works, we found irregular period changes in $\sim$33% of Magellanic classical Cepheids, but excluded Cepheids showing additional low-amplitude variability. Here, we establish whether first-overtone Cepheids hosting such variability differ in their period-change behaviour from the general first-overtone population. We analyse 544 Magellanic Cepheids with period ratios $P_{\rm x}/P_{\rm 1O} \sim 0.60-0.65$ or $P_{\rm 1O}/P_{\rm x} \sim 0.68$, using OGLE photometry, and classify and characterise their O-C diagrams following our previous studies. We find irregular period changes in 339 first-overtone Cepheids (195 in the LMC and 144 in the SMC), an incidence rate of $\sim$75.5%, a statistically significant increase over the $\sim$68.1% of our previous single-mode first-overtone sample. The combined first-overtone incidence becomes $\sim$69.7%. This provides the first empirical connection between additional low-amplitude variability and irregular period changes in first-overtone Cepheids. At a fixed pulsation period, the irregularity strength anticorrelates with the dominant pulsation amplitude but not with the additional-signal amplitude, suggesting that the additional periodicity marks a weakly saturated pulsation state rather than driving the irregularity. We further detect cycle-to-cycle (C2C) period variation in 37% of the class 3 sample, with jitter roughly seven times larger than in non-Blazhko RRc stars and a shallower scaling with pulsation period.

entries.title: Starspots on eclipsing giant stars II.: TESS continuous viewing zone giant V521 Dra
entries.abstract: Eclipsing binaries are exceptional laboratories for stellar astrophysics. By analysing the modulations in their eclipse light curves, we can probe their surface inhomogeneities. The eclipse-mapping technique enables us to scan starspots in detail, using the transit of a companion star across the surface of a spotted star. When multiple consecutive eclipses are observed, this method may also reveal the evolution of spot properties and provide evidence for stellar differential rotation. We study the magnetic activity of V521 Dra, a tidally locked eclipsing binary with a red giant primary and a main-sequence secondary, both of K spectral class, on a 4.27 d orbit. This is an exceptional system with ~5.3 years of TESS 2 min cadence observations. This offers a unique opportunity to study magnetic activity in uninterrupted blocks over several years with very high photometric precision. We aim to constrain the evolution of the spot pattern of V521 Dra A. We used two methods to study the spot activity of the primary: eclipse mapping and analytic spot modelling. We analysed the stellar properties of the system with a set of methods, including combined modelling of the eclipse light curves, radial velocity data, spectral energy distribution analysis, and forward modelling of the whole orbital light curve. The star shows strong spot-induced modulations both in the eclipse and out-of-eclipse parts of the light curve. We identified 540 spot eclipse signals in 203 primary eclipses. Eclipse mapping reveals the presence of up to four spots. The spot longitudes drift continuously in time, indicating differential rotation. Spots in the eclipse-mapping data show differing angular velocities in their drift, implying a near-surface shear in the convective zone of the primary. Using time series spectroscopy and the spectral energy distribution, we constrained the astrophysical parameters of the binary system.

entries.title: AGB Atmospheres in Binary Environments: A First Step with CO5BOLB
entries.abstract: Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are characterized by complex atmospheric dynamics driven by convection and pulsations. In binary systems, the presence of a companion can further influence these dynamics, potentially affecting mass-loss processes and the morphology of the circumstellar environment, yet this influence on the atmosphere itself remains poorly quantified. This study aims to fill this gap by employing CO5BOLD simulations with a modified gravitational potential to explore how companion mass affects the atmospheric structure of AGB stars. We used radiative hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations with CO5BOLD to model the convective interior and atmosphere of AGB stars. We modified the gravitational potential to include a secondary mass and a centrifugal term, representing the companion as a point-mass potential on a steady, tidally locked circular orbit outside the computational domain, with the Coriolis force neglected. We performed simulations with different companion masses and using singular value decomposition (SVD), we identified the spatial distribution of pulsation energy and quantified its properties. We also examined the density structure to identify anisotropies induced by the companion. We isolate two dynamically distinct regimes, a pulsation-dominated layer and an outer, low-frequency outflow region, whose pulsation properties remain largely unaffected by the companion: their frequency, amplitude, and coherence stay consistent across all models. The density structure, by contrast, responds clearly to the companion, forming a pronounced anisotropy along the binary axis that strengthens with companion mass. This indicates that the intrinsic pulsational dynamics of the AGB star dominate over the tidal influence of the companion within the explored parameter space, while the density structure remains the most sensitive tracer of binarity.

entries.title: Bidimensional Exploration of the warm-Temperature Ionised gaS (BETIS) III. The impact of eDIG on strong-line abundance determinations in galactic halos
entries.abstract: The extraplanar diffuse ionised gas (eDIG) is a key tracer of the feedback processes that connect galactic discs and halos. We present the first study of spatially resolved gas-phase chemical abundances in the eDIG of edge-on galaxies, based on integral field spectroscopy obtained with MUSE. Using a sample of four galaxies from the BETIS sample, we derived maps of the oxygen abundance, 12+log(O/H), the nitrogen-to-oxygen ratio, log(N/O), and the ionisation parameter, log(U), with the HII-CHI-Mistry v5.5 code, and we tested the reliability of this method when different ionisation sources are present. We separated the eDIG into star-formation-dominated and shock-contaminated regimes according to the relative contribution of photoionisation and shocks, and investigated their impact on the derived chemical abundances. We find that HII-CHI-Mistry returns systematically lower O/H and N/O values in shock-contaminated regions, especially for N/O, with typical offsets of ~0.1-0.15 dex relative to star-formation-dominated regions, together with a more homogeneous and lower ionisation state (log(U) ~ -3.1). In contrast, star-formation-dominated regions span a wider range of ionisation parameters (log(U) ~ -3.3 to -2.8) while maintaining approximately solar oxygen abundances. Despite these differences, the abundance offsets are comparable to the sampling step of the HII-CHI-Mistry model grid. The inferred oxygen abundance shows little variation between discs and halos. This is compatible with a scenario in which star formation feedback and galactic fountains efficiently recycle oxygen-rich gas between both components, in agreement with hydrodynamical simulations. In contrast, the N/O ratio shows significant radial and vertical variations, particularly in environments with weaker star formation feedback.

entries.title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
entries.abstract: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

entries.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
entries.abstract: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

entries.title: The ultraviolet continuum slopes of galaxies at $\mathbf{z \gtrsim 12}$ selected from ${\mathbf{0.6 \, deg}^2}$ of JWST imaging
entries.abstract: We present an analysis of the ultraviolet (UV) continuum slopes $(β)$ of $55$ galaxies at $z\gtrsim 12$, selected from a wide-area ($>0.6$ sq. deg) search across publicly available JWST/NIRCam imaging. Our sample spans the absolute UV magnitude ($M_{\mathrm{UV}}$) range $-21.6 \leq M_{\mathrm{UV}} \leq -17.3$ and we find an inverse variance-weighted mean $\langleβ\rangle = -2.57\pm0.04$ indicating that, on average, the galaxy population is extremely blue at $z\gtrsim 12$. The average $β$ at these redshifts is consistent with the intrinsic stellar plus nebular continuum limit in the absence of UV dust-attenuation. Consistent with earlier JWST works, our analysis suggests that the moderately dust-attenuated galaxies at $z \lesssim 10$ become essentially attenuation-free by $z \simeq 11$. We find no evidence for a $β-M_{\mathrm{UV}}$ relation in our $z\gtrsim 12$ sample, indicating that the attenuation-free interpretation applies across all observed UV magnitudes. By augmenting our sample with previous JWST constraints down to $z=9$, and incorporating $M_{\mathrm{UV}}$-matched HST studies down to $z=4$, we find a smooth evolution in $β(z)$ over a wide range in redshift. The average value of $β$ becomes progressively bluer at $z>4$, with $\mathrm{d}β/\mathrm{d}z \simeq -0.1$. Finally, although we find that the typical galaxy at $z \gtrsim 12$ is consistent with the attenuation-free limit, the scatter in our individual $β$ measurements is consistent with the existence of a small population of dust-reddened galaxies with $β\gtrsim -2$.

entries.title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
entries.abstract: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

entries.title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
entries.abstract: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

entries.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
entries.abstract: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $ν_τ$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

entries.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
entries.abstract: White dwarfs (WDs) provide a fossil record of the Milky Way star formation history (SFH) through the combined effects of stellar evolution and cooling. They have, however, generally been modelled in isolation from the non-degenerate population, so that no single self-consistent set of Galactic assumptions has been required to reproduce both. We present CALOMERA, a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population synthesis framework in which the vertical density profiles of mono-age subpopulations are computed self-consistently with the Galactic potential and coupled to modern WD cooling sequences, metallicity-dependent progenitor lifetimes and synthetic photometry. We calibrate 18 parameters describing the initial mass function, SFH, initial-final mass relation and WD population against a Gaia DR3 sample of $7.98\times10^{6}$ stars within 1 kpc, including $1.1\times10^{5}$ WDs. The calibrated model reproduces the star counts in each colour-magnitude diagram region to within 3% and the total number count to within 0.5%, compared with the 81% excess in the predicted WD count obtained with the previous main-sequence-only calibration. The recovered SFH peaks early, declines exponentially thereafter, and includes two recent bursts, located at $τ\approx2.4$ and $0.5$ Gyr. Three cooling libraries (Montréal, BaSTI and LPCODE) yield comparably good fits, with differences confined to ${\rm M_G}\gtrsim15$ mag. The predicted luminosity function is in reasonable agreement with the 100 pc Gaia WD sample. We further predict the Galactic WD distribution and differential number counts for surveys of varying depth. Extending the framework to the substellar regime using ATMO models, we predict the Galactic L, T, and Y dwarf populations and their contribution to the deep JWST fields.

analysis.reason: This review directly links young-supernova X-rays to progenitor winds, shock–CSM interaction, and pre-explosion mass-loss history, and it provides scaling relations that can test those hypotheses.
analysis.result: Wind density follows $\rho_w\propto\dot{M}/v_w$. In the Chevalier (1982) model, $\rho_{\mathrm{SN}}=\rho_0(v/v_0)^{-n}(t/t_0)^{-3}$, $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto r^{-s}$ with $s=2$ for a steady wind, and $R_{\mathrm{CD}}\propto t^m$ where $m=(n-3)/(n-s)\le1$. For spherical progenitors with $9\le n\le12$, steady-wind thermal $L_x$ falls roughly as $t^{-0.7}$–$t^{-0.8}$ and approaches $t^{-1}$ at larger $n$. The order-of-magnitude luminosity is $L_i=3\times10^{39}g_{ff}C_n(\dot{M}_{-5}/v_{w1})^2(t/10\,\mathrm{d})^{-1}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, with $C_n=1$ for the forward shock and $C_n=(n-3)(n-4)^2/[4(n-2)]$ for the reverse shock; observations constrain $\dot{M}/v_w$. RSG/IIP rates are $\dot{M}\approx10^{-8}$–$10^{-6}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, while WR Ib/c winds have $v_w\approx1000$–$3000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Many sources show only $1$–$2\,\mathrm{keV}$, below $\sim40\,\mathrm{keV}$ expected for a $\sim5000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ forward shock, favoring reverse-shock emission. SN 1993J has early $\dot{M}>10^{-5}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$; inverse-Compton modeling with $N(E)\propto E^{-p}$ at $p=3$ gives SN 2011ja $(1.2\pm0.2)\times10^{-7}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$; SN 2011dh is an adiabatic reverse shock with $\dot{M}$ of a few $\times10^{-6}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Thermal X-rays are directly proportional to circumstellar density, and a radiative reverse shock can coexist with a non-radiative forward shock.

analysis.problem: The core problem is how X-rays from a young supernova shock expanding in a progenitor wind, rather than pristine ISM, can recover the progenitor mass-loss rate, wind velocity, and CSM density structure despite shock-type and geometry degeneracies.
analysis.method: The analysis uses the Chevalier self-similar shock solution, with ambient density $\rho_{am}=\dot{M}(r_0/r)^s/(4\pi r_0^2 v_w)$, thermal-luminosity scalings for adiabatic and radiative shocks, inverse-Compton spectra $N(E)\propto E^{-p}$, and multiwavelength checks. Radio light curves are fit with Chevalier/Weiler relations to estimate $\dot{M}/v_w$, while optical/IR/UV emission is compared using $L_{\mathrm{opt/IR/UV}}=0.5\,\epsilon\,(\dot{M}/v_w)\,v_{\mathrm{sh}}^3$; X-ray light curves and spectra are preferred because self-similar evolution gives $v\propto t^{m-1}$.
limits: The inferred timing of pre-death wind changes spans hundreds to thousands of years and depends on the adopted wind velocity.

It also distinguishes direct thermal-density constraints from indirect nonthermal and clump-sensitive optical diagnostics.

figures.caption: Figure 8: The interaction of a SN shock wave with an equatorial torus, as may have happened in SN 2014c. The plot shows the density structure from a simulation carried out by the author to study the shock interaction with the equatorial torus in SN 2014c. The VH-1 numerical hydrodynamics code was used Dwarkadas et al. (1996); Dwarkadas and Balick (1998); Dwarkadas (2005); Dwarkadas (2007); Dwarkadas et al. (2010). The impact with the torus drives a transmitted shock into the torus, and a reflected shock back into the ejecta. The shock above and below the torus expands in a lower-density He-rich wind, and therefore, has a much higher velocity. The radio emission arises from this shock. The H $\alpha$ emission arises from the transmitted shock in the torus. The reflected shock and reverse shock in the He-rich wind tend to converge at a point.

figures.caption: Figure 6: The density structure of the medium around SN 1987A in the equatorial plane, using a simulation that combines the photo-ionizing photons from the central pre-SN star with the hydrodynamics of the wind bubble evolution. The inclusion of the stellar photons results in the formation of a dense photo-ionized HII region interior to the shell. Going outwards in radius from the central star, the various regions are (1) the freely expanding wind, (2) the shocked wind, (3) the photo-ionized (HII) region, (4) the dense swept-up shell (equatorial ring) and (5) the red-supergiant wind from the previous epoch. Details of the simulation and the modeling technique are described in Dwarkadas (2022).

analysis.reason: This statistical afterglow study directly constrains sGRB jet energy and the horizon magnetic field of BNS-merger black holes, which is central to relativistic-jet and compact-remnant engine physics. The reported $E_{\rm k}$, $\eta_\gamma$ and $B_{\rm BH}$ distributions can test whether a Blandford–Znajek engine is viable.
analysis.result: For the 15 strictly constrained (SC) bursts, the median on-axis energy is $\log E_0=52.54$ (68% interval $[51.08,53.43]$), i.e. $E_0\simeq 3.5\times 10^{52}\,\mathrm{erg}$. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy has median $\log E_{\rm k}=49.58$, or $E_{\rm k}\simeq 3.8\times 10^{49}\,\mathrm{erg}$ (68% interval $[5.1\times 10^{48},1.9\times 10^{50}]\,\mathrm{erg}$), and the radiative efficiency has median $\eta_\gamma\simeq 0.35$ (68% interval $[0.09,0.79]$), where $\eta_\gamma=E_\gamma/(E_\gamma+E_{\rm k})$ and $\Gamma_0=300$. Under the BZ scaling $\frac{L_{\rm k}}{1-\eta_\gamma}\approx 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}\left(\frac{a}{0.9}\right)^2\left(\frac{M_{\rm BH}}{5\,M_\odot}\right)^2\left(\frac{B_{\rm BH}}{10^{16}\,\mathrm{G}}\right)^2$, the SC horizon field is $B_{\rm BH}\simeq 7\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ ($7.1^{+15.8}_{-4.8}\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ and $7.2^{+16.3}_{-4.9}\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ for the two $\tilde\Lambda$ cases), with amplification $\eta_B\equiv B_{\rm BH}/B_{\rm NS}$ of order $10^3$ (medians $1463$ and $1026$). For all 40 bursts the medians shift to $\log(E_0/\mathrm{erg})=52.35$, $\log(E_{\rm k}/\mathrm{erg})=50.20$, $\eta_\gamma=0.26$ and $B_{\rm BH}\sim 2\times 10^{16}\,\mathrm{G}$ ($\log(B_{\rm BH}/\mathrm{G})=16.31$–$16.36$).
analysis.problem: The paper asks what beaming-corrected kinetic energies and gamma-ray efficiencies characterize cosmological short GRBs from BNS mergers, and what black-hole horizon field is required if the Blandford–Znajek process supplies most of the jet energy.
analysis.method: Forty sGRBs with reliable redshifts (Gold Sample, $P_{\rm cc}<0.02$) are fitted burst by burst with an off-axis truncated Gaussian jet in a uniform ISM using afterglowpy, retaining only forward-shock points after removing intervals possibly affected by energy injection, flares, reverse shocks or kilonovae. The angular structure and beam-corrected energy are $E(\theta)=E_0\exp(-\theta^2/2\theta_{\rm c}^2)$ and $E_{\rm k}=E_0\theta_{\rm c}^2\left(1-e^{-\theta_{\rm w}^2/2\theta_{\rm c}^2}\right)$, while $E_{\gamma,\mathrm{iso}}=k\times 4\pi d_{\rm L}^2 f_\gamma/(1+z)$ with a population-mean $k=5$ when the spectrum is unavailable. The 15 SC posteriors supply empirical priors for the other 25 bursts. Jet power is then mapped to the horizon field through $L_{\rm BZ}=\frac{\kappa}{4\pi c}\Omega_{\rm H}^2\Phi_{\rm BH}^2 f(\Omega_{\rm H})$ with $\kappa\sim 0.05$, $\Omega_{\rm H}=ac/(2r_{\rm H})$, $E_{\rm BZ}=E_{\rm k}+E_\gamma$ and $L_{\rm k}\equiv E_{\rm k}/T_{90}$.
assumptions: Magnetic-field constraints assume that a predominantly Blandford–Znajek-powered jet supplies most of the sGRB energy.
Only forward-shock data are fitted, after removal of intervals that may contain additional energy injection or other non-FS components.
limits: The derived horizon fields are conditional on BZ powering and do not exclude magnetar spin-down or neutrino-annihilation engines.
Sparse non-SC afterglows leave $\theta_{\rm c}$, $\theta_{\rm w}$ and $\theta_{\rm obs}$ degenerate, so the full-sample $E_{\rm k}$ and $\eta_\gamma$ distributions differ from the SC results.
An NSBH jet requires tidal disruption of the NS outside the ISCO; most NSBH mergers are argued to contribute little electromagnetic contamination.
